summary.one_liner: Notable is a very simple, local note-taking application written in Go that ships as a static binary with a browser-based interface.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a note app with no external dependencies that stores everything locally on the user's computer. Individual notes can be encrypted. Search works as you type, covering tags, tag prefixes, and full text via a full-text index. It supports autosave per note, shows unsaved changes visually, and can re-index on demand (useful for backup and restore). Multiple notes can be opened in tabs, and keyboard shortcuts are available (help via the ? key). The README lists Linux, FreeBSD, MacOS, and Windows (experimental) as platforms, and says distributed writes via Keybase and Syncthing are experimental.
use_cases: search notes by tag or full text
run a local notes server in Docker
sync notes across machines with Syncthing or Keybase
how_to_run: Download and extract the latest release zip, then run the included `notable` executable
notable: Ships as a static binary with no dependencies
Search-as-you-type over tags, tag prefixes, and full text
Experimental sync via Keybase and Syncthing
Makefile targets for test, vet, iterate, and Docker builds
caveats: Distributed writes (Keybase, Syncthing) are marked experimental
The README does not describe a hosted or multi-user service
